about: The desktop app's downloads. The one switch is `available`: while it is false nothing on the site offers a download — /download/ exists but is linked from nowhere, carries noindex and shows the one-command start; the home section and the footer's Download link stay off. Set it to true once at least one platform below has `available: true` and a real `url`; a platform that isn't available is listed as coming, never as a button. `url` is the file's direct address (a release asset); `size` is as people read it ("92 MB"); `requires` is the oldest system it runs on, in words; `signed` false makes the page say plainly that the app isn't signed yet and show `open`, the steps past the system's warning (markdown: **bold** for what to click, `code` for commands). `also` lists other files for the same platform. `screens` are captures of the app window in public/screens (<src>.webp + <src>@1x.webp, 2×): one without its file, or without alt text written after looking at it, is left out — never a stand-in. The first screen with `home: true` is the one on the home page. Statuses stay in status.json; CLAIMS.md says what supports each line.

platforms.label: Mac with Apple silicon
open: Open the downloaded `.dmg` and drag **Galley** into **Applications**.
In **Applications**, right-click **Galley**, choose **Open**, then **Open** again in the window that asks.
If macOS still won’t open it, go to **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, find the line about Galley and choose **Open Anyway**.

platforms.label: Mac with an Intel processor
open: Open the downloaded `.dmg` and drag **Galley** into **Applications**.
In **Applications**, right-click **Galley**, choose **Open**, then **Open** again in the window that asks.

platforms.label: Windows
open: If Windows says it protected your PC, choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
Follow the installer, then open **Galley** from the Start menu.

platforms.label: Linux
open: Let the downloaded `.AppImage` run as a program: in its **Properties**, allow executing it — or run `chmod +x` on it in a terminal.
